title: Where harmfulness lives and where refusal is decided: one-word harmful/harmless twins under real, hypothetical, roleplay, fiction, nested and depicted frames
why: exp114 found the real/fiction frame is encoded but the content inside it reads the same. Models still refuse many harmful requests in fiction. Published work reports that harmfulness and refusal are encoded separately, and that jailbreaks lower refusal while harmfulness stays recognised. This tests that on our model with matched twins, locates both, and ties in exp117's concept surgery.

design.model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B (plain, NOT abliterated: abliteration removes the refusal direction), bf16, MPS, chat template, enable_thinking=False.
design.stimuli: 24 everyday-wrongdoing requests, each with a harmless twin differing in one word (stimuli.py; no weapons, drugs, CBRN, self-harm or sexual content). 6 frames: real, hypothetical, roleplay, fiction (an expert answers in a story), nested (fiction + 'this isn't really for a story, I actually need to know'), depict (a story in which a man does the act; no how-to). The request text is token-identical across the five request frames.
design.no_generation: Nothing is generated. Refusal score = logsumexp over REFUSE reply prefixes - logsumexp over COMPLY prefixes (stimuli.py), each prefix's log-probability by teacher forcing at the reply's first position.
design.positions: word = the twin word's last sub-token; inst = last token of the user message; post = last prompt token (the reply onset, after the empty think block).
design.directions: Fitted on the real frame only, cross-fitted over halves of the items (even/odd), evaluated on the held-out half. h (harmfulness) = mean(harmful) - mean(harmless) at inst. r (refusal) = mean(harmful) - mean(harmless) at post (the Arditi et al. construction). Layers 2..34 step 4, plus 18; tests at layer 18. 'Request span' = mean over the request tokens.

hypotheses.H1_harm_decodable: Harmful vs harmless twins separate at post with leave-item-out AUC >= 0.90 at layer 18 (diff-of-means probe, real frame). Descriptive: the first layer reaching 0.90 at word, inst and post.
hypotheses.H2_refusal_control: In the real frame the refusal score is higher for harmful than for harmless twins (paired one-sided Wilcoxon over the 24 items). This is the positive control: if it fails, H4-H7 are reported as uninformative.
hypotheses.H3_harm_frame_invariant: The h-projection of the request span (layer 18) for harmful items in fiction equals that in real within +/- 0.25 x the real harmful-minus-harmless gap (TOST, alpha 0.05).
hypotheses.H4_refusal_frame_sensitive: From real to fiction, the refusal score of harmful items drops by a larger share of its real harmful-minus-harmless gap than the h-projection does (paired one-sided Wilcoxon over items on the two normalised drops).
hypotheses.H5_refusal_tracks_r: Over harmful items x the five request frames, Spearman(refusal score, r-projection at post) exceeds Spearman(refusal score, h-projection of the request span). Bootstrap over items (1000), 95% CI of the difference above 0.
hypotheses.H6_depicted_less_refused: Harmful items: refusal score in depict < in fiction (paired one-sided Wilcoxon). The model treats depicting an act differently from explaining it inside a story.
hypotheses.H7_nested_restores: Harmful items: refusal score in nested > in fiction (paired one-sided Wilcoxon). A plain statement of real intent inside the fiction frame raises refusal.

corrections: H1, H3-H7 Holm-corrected as one family (H2 is the control). Layer sweeps are descriptive.
decision_rule: 'Harmfulness is separate from refusal, and fiction acts on refusal' is SUPPORTED if H3, H4 and H5 all hold. It is REFUTED if H3 fails because harmful-in-fiction reads as less harmful by more than the margin AND H5 fails. Otherwise mixed.

exploratory.E1_surgery: exp117 concept surgery at block 8, alpha 1, full difference, at the twin word: in harmful real prompts, swap harm word -> benign word; in harmless real prompts, benign -> harm. Concept states from exp117's 6 neutral sentences. Measure the change in refusal score and in r at post. Random-direction control of equal norm. Question: is the harm carried by the concept variable at the word?
exploratory.E2_boost: Add alpha x r (alpha in 0.5, 1, 2, in units of the real-frame gap's norm) at post only, at one layer (10, 14, 18). Measure refusal score on harmful items in fiction / depict (want: up) and on harmless items in every frame (over-refusal; want: flat). Same with h added over the request span. Question: which push raises refusal selectively for harmful requests in fiction without making the model refuse harmless ones?

notes: Smoke run (EXP119_N=3) checks code only and is discarded.
